title: Structural and biophysical characterization of the nucleosome-binding PZP domain
protocol: Transform plasmids into Rosetta-2 (DE3) pLysS chemically competent cells.
Inoculate a single colony from LB agar supplemented with ampicillin and chloramphenicol into 250 ml of LB preculture containing the same antibiotics in a 1 L flask.
Grow the preculture for 14–18 hours at 37°C and 180–200 rpm on a shaker.
In a 6 L Erlenmeyer flask containing M9 Minimal Media, add ampicillin (100 μg/mL), chloramphenicol (34 μg/mL), glucose, and vitamin.
Transfer the flask to an Innova 4330 floor shaker prewarmed to 37°C and shake at 200 rpm.
When the optical density reaches 0.6–0.8 at an absorbance of 600 nm, reduce the temperature and speed to 16°C and 180 rpm, respectively.
Add isopropyl β-d-1-thiogalactopyranoside (IPTG) to a final concentration of 0.5 mM when the temperature reaches 16°C–19°C.
Express protein at 16°C for 18 hours.
Add zinc chloride (ZnCl2) between 20-30 μM along with IPTG during induction to increase yield.
Harvest the cultures and collect cell pellets by centrifugation in a F10-6 × 500y Fixed-Angle Rotor in a floor centrifuge for 10 min at 4,400 × g and 10°C.
Resuspend cells in PZP Purification Buffer A using a beaker.
Stir the resuspended cells on a stir plate with a stir bar for complete resuspension for 10–30 min at 4°C.
Sonicate the suspended cells on ice for 5 min using settings of 60% power with intervals of 5 s on and 10 s off.
Mix cells and repeat sonication step.
Centrifuge the cell suspension in balanced 50 mL Nalgene Oak Ridge High-Speed PPCO Centrifuge tubes at 27,000 × g using a SS-34 Fixed Angle Rotor at 4°C–10°C for 30 min.
Gently collect the supernatant without disturbing the pellet containing cell debris and insoluble fraction.
Combine the collected supernatant with equilibrated glutathione beads in a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Place the tube on a rocker at low-medium speed for 1 hour at 4°C.
Wash the beads using PZP Purification Buffer B (50 mM Tris pH 7.5, 500 mM NaCl, and 5 mM DTT).
Take a 15 μL sample of the beads for analysis by SDS polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis.
Bring the volume in the tube containing the beads up to 15–20 mL with PZP Purification Buffer B.
Add TEV enzyme (14 mg/mL, 30 μL) and gently rock on a platform shaker set to level 2-3 for 15–20 hours at 4°C.
Pour a 1.5 mm mini gel cassette with a 15% SDS polyacrylamide gel.
Prepare 4× SDS loading buffer consisting of 200 mM Tris-HCl (pH 6.8), 400 mM DTT, 8% w/v SDS, 0.4% w/v bromophenol blue, and 40% v/v glycerol.
Heat samples at 90°C for 10 minutes to denature proteins.
Spin down samples for 5-10 seconds at 5,000 × g in an Eppendorf Microcentrifuge 5424R.
Load samples onto the gel and run until the dye front reaches the bottom of the gel.
Elute protein contained in the supernatant once desired cleavage is obtained (75%-90%).
Concentrate the eluted protein to 2 mL using a 10,000 Da MWCO centrifugal filter at 3,000 × g.
Inject concentrated protein into a HiPrep™ 16/60 Sephacryl® S-100 HR column equilibrated with Purification Buffer B.
Run the column at 0.2 mL/min in 4°C until approximately 66 mL has eluted.
Verify and select pure fractions through SDS PAGE as per initial step.
Pool selected fractions and concentrate to a final concentration of 20-40 mg/mL using a 10,000 Da MWCO centrifugal filter at 3,000 × g.
Gently thaw purified 15N-labeled BRPF1PZP on ice.
Centrifuge the sample at 15,000 × g in an Eppendorf Microcentrifuge 5424R and separate the supernatant from any debris or precipitation.
Check the protein concentration using NanoDrop 2000c with Bradford solution and a standard curve using BSA at known concentrations.
Determine the unknown concentration of BRPF1PZP protein using the standard curve.
Compare the calculated protein concentration by Bradford solution to that found using the extinction coefficient determined from the protein sequence.
Dilute protein to 0.1–0.2 mM using Purification Buffer C (50 mM Tris pH 7.5 and 5 mM DTT).
Add Purification Buffer D (50 mM Tris pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, and 5 mM DTT) to bring the salt concentration of the buffer to 150 mM NaCl.
Combine 198 μL sample with 22 μL of D2O (final concentration of 10%).
Gently mix the combined solution up and down using a pipette.
Using a glass pipette, gently pipette the mixture into a shigemi tube.
Insert the plunger into the shigemi tube and remove all bubbles by gently rotating the plunger up and down.
Seal the shigemi tube with parafilm.
Record 1H,15N heteronuclear single quantum coherence (HSQC) spectra of the apo-state of the protein at 298K on a Varian INOVA 600 MHz NMR spectrometer.
Add increasing amounts of histone H3 peptide to the NMR sample and record 1H,15N HSQC spectra after each addition until saturation is reached.
Process the recorded spectra using NMRPipe software.
Overlay the spectra to analyze chemical shift perturbations induced in BRPF1PZP.
Concentrate H3-GSGSS-BRPF1PZP protein to greater than 20 mg/mL in Purification Buffer B.
Dilute concentrated protein to approximately 6 mg/mL using Purification Buffer C.
Spin down the diluted protein at 15,000 × g to remove any precipitation.
Set up crystal drops for H3-GSGSS-BRPF1PZP by combining 0.6 μL of protein with 0.6 μL of well solution.
Grow crystals using the sitting-drop diffusion method at 18°C.
Collect crystallization data sets and determine the structure of the complex.
Add 1.2 μL of a 60% (v/v) glycerol solution directly to the drop.
Maintain a final concentration of 30% (v/v) glycerol in the drop.
Loop the crystal with an appropriate loop size.
Mount the crystal directly on the homesource instrument.
Add additional well and glycerol solution if the drop dries out slightly, maintaining 30% (v/v) glycerol.
Freeze crystals in liquid nitrogen for storage or shipping to a synchrotron.
Collect X-ray diffraction data sets using a Rigaku Micromax 007 high-frequency microfocus X-ray generator.
Use HKL3000 program to complete the indexing, integration and scaling of the data set.
Determine the initial structure by molecular replacement using apo BRPF1pzp (PDB ID: 5ERC) as a model in Phenix Phaser.
Carry out manual model building with Coot.
Refine the structure using Phenix.
Validate the structure with MolProbity.
Check the quality of the model and experimental data using Worldwide Protein Data Bank OneDep SYSTEM.
Fix any issues identified in the validation report.
Use the validation report to determine if a ligand needs further work or if protein side chains are incorrect.
Deposit data with the Worldwide Protein Data Bank OneDep SYSTEM.
Record the PDB ID.
Prepare EMSA reaction buffer for BRPF1PZP running samples.
Dilute NCPs in 0.5× TE and store on ice.
Make 12 μL of each BRPF1PZP sample at concentrations of 150, 100, 50, 30, 10, 3, and 1 μM from the protein stock.
Prepare 20 μL of 30 nM NCPs.
Mix BRPF1PZP samples with NCP and incubate at 4°C for 15 min.
Combine 2 μL of NCPs with 10 μL of each BRPF1PZP sample to start the reactions.
For zero BRPF1PZP concentration, add 10 μL of Reaction Buffer instead.
Load reaction mixtures onto a gel and run electrophoresis at 300V for 1.5 h in 0.3× TBE buffer.
Prepare BRPF1PZP samples using fluorescence polarization reaction buffer.
Dilute NCPs in 0.5× TE and store on ice.
Prepare 30 μL of 150, 100, 50, 30, 10, 3, and 1 μM BRPF1PZP running samples from the protein stock.
Prepare 70 μL of 50 nM NCPs.
Mix 3 μL of NCP with 27 μL of BRPF1PZP samples to start the reactions.
For zero BRPF1PZP concentration, use 27 μL of reaction buffer instead.
For background measurements, use 3 μL of 0.5× TE instead of the NCP sample.
Place reaction mixtures into wells of the Costar black plate.
Load plate into the Tecan plate reader.
Initialize i-control and use the fluorescence module to measure fluorescence polarization by exciting samples with 470 nm polarized light and measuring emission at 520 nm (for fluorescein).
Make sure the protocol outputs raw data of the polarized emission light intensity parallel and perpendicular to the plane of excitation.
Run the protocol.
Monitor the quality of free histone or short oligonucleosomes by Coomassie staining before HAT assays.
Mix free histone or short oligonucleosome with 3 μl of purified BRPF1 complex, 3 μl of HAT buffer 5×, 1 mM Na butyrate and 50 mM of KCl or NaCl.
Keep the reaction mixture on ice for 15 min.
Add 0.125 μCi of 3H labeled Ac-CoA (0.1 mCi/mL).
Incubate the mixture at 30°C for 30 min.
Spot the reactions on P81 filter paper.
Air dry the filter paper.
Wash the filter paper 3 times in 50 mM carbonate buffer (NaHCO3–NaCO3, pH 9.2).
Rinse the filter paper rapidly with acetone.
Air dry the filter paper again.
Place the filter paper in a scintillation tube.
Add scintillation cocktail to the filter paper in the scintillation tube.
Measure counts in a scintillation counter for 30 min.
